utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Good morning, sir. Your affirmation still applies. I have learnt overnight that it is important for the witness to be able to finish today. I did, without knowledge of that, urge counsel to give attention only to the important things today. That news reinforces that. We have seen with some other witnesses how effective that can be. I would ask the cooperation of counsel in achieving that objective. Mr. Domazet.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOMAZET
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Good afternoon, Your Honours. Good afternoon to all. Good afternoon, sir. I'll pick up where I left off yesterday. You were answering my questions and you were talking about the events unfolding in Vukovar in the spring of 1991, your personal experience as well as that of your family. You talked about the telephone calls, the threats you received and warnings to leave town. Do you know about anybody else being subjected to such threats, or was this simply an unpleasant topic to discuss at the time?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-009 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I heard that other people got such telephone phone calls, and the threats that -- that I mentioned yesterday, yes. That's fine. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOMAZET
utterances.text: Your mother, I assume, was not involved in politics and did not hold any political post in your community, or your father for that matter? You yourself, after all, were only 19 years of age at the time, weren't you?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-009 [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's correct, sir. That's exactly right. Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOMAZET
utterances.text: You explained that this was the reason that you decided for the first time to leave Vukovar with your mother, sometime in July 1991. First you went to Belgrade and then to Bijeljina. Your father joined you in Belgrade a little later. My question: During your time in Belgrade, did you personally or your father as an ethnic Hungarian encounter any problems or any friction in that environment?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-009 [Resumed]
utterances.text: [Previous translation continues] ... say that anything happened there, no.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOMAZET
utterances.text: After that you left for Bijeljina. You talked about the better living conditions and about the fact that Vukovar was now closer. How about your time in Sid, though? You said you went there to see a friend. Was that the real reason behind your decision, and if so, who was that friend in Sid?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-009 [Resumed]
utterances.text: One of my friends from the same -- same home town where I used to live was as a refugee in Sid, so I decided to go there. I didn't see any reason why not. Why wouldn't I be able to go there?

utterances.speaker: MR. DOMAZET
utterances.text: Did you know at the time that there was a recruitment and mobilisation office in Sid for people who hail from Vukovar and a Territorial Defence office for Eastern Slavonia?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-009 [Resumed]
utterances.text: [Previous translation continues] ... territorial mobilisation, but I assume that there was -- there were armies over there, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOMAZET
utterances.text: If you had known this, would you still have decided to run the risk all the same and go to Sid to see your friend?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-009 [Resumed]
utterances.text: [Previous translation continues] ...

utterances.speaker: MR. DOMAZET
utterances.text: My apologies. Can I ask you to please repeat your answer, because it wasn't recorded. Your last answer?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-009 [Resumed]
utterances.text: [Previous translation continues] ...

utterances.speaker: MR. DOMAZET
utterances.text: Your acquaintance if I may call him that --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Mr. Domazet, we still didn't get the answer because the witness answered you while you were still speaking. We've just got to get back into that habit of watching. The answer twice was "probably not."

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: That's correct, sir.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Now, Mr. Smith.

utterances.speaker: MR. SMITH
utterances.text: Just briefly, Your Honour. In relation to page 3, line 25, a question was put and it's the similar problem as you have just mentioned. Then we have the answer at page 3, line 3, the witness's answer which wasn't recorded was that he wasn't aware that there was a recruitment and mobilisation office, so it just reflects the problem.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Thank you. Mr. Domazet.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOMAZET
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. DOMAZET
utterances.text: You said person A was an acquaintance of yours. He practically tricked you into going to that building where the mobilisation office was, right?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-009 [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's correct, sir, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOMAZET
utterances.text: You mentioned that there was yet another person with them whom you also said you knew. Can you tell us who that was?

utterances.speaker: MR. SMITH
utterances.text: Your Honour, I would just ask that this be in private session, if he provides the name.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Private.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOMAZET
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. DOMAZET
utterances.text: You described the Velepromet warehouse in Vukovar. You went into a lot of detail about that. Based on what you saw when you were there, did it strike you that the warehouse might have been used as a logistics base by the TO people?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-009 [Resumed]
utterances.text: You mean when I was brought first time or after that?

utterances.speaker: MR. DOMAZET
utterances.text: I mean generally. How did it look to you, the first time you were there as well as later on? You must have had a chance to have a look, have a good look. What was the impression you had?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-009 [Resumed]
utterances.text: First time I was over there, I didn't have that kind of impression. I wasn't really sure what it was. There were soldiers there, but I didn't know, was that a command post or was it a -- I don't know, warehouse for the -- for the army or whatever it is. No, I wasn't aware of that. No.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOMAZET
utterances.text: Zigic, the man who met you there, was he one of the commanders for those people there, or is that at least what it looked like?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-009 [Resumed]
utterances.text: [Previous translation continues] ...

utterances.speaker: MR. DOMAZET
utterances.text: Can you please repeat the last answer?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-009 [Resumed]
utterances.text: That was my general understanding, sir.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOMAZET
utterances.text: You mentioned that there was another person with him. You later learned that this person was Vujovic's body-guard, and Vujovic is a person whom you believed to be one of the TO commanders there. Would I be right in stating that?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-009 [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's correct, sir.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOMAZET
utterances.text: Did you know Vujovic from before, from before the war?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-009 [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, sir, I didn't know.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOMAZET
utterances.text: Since you didn't know him, did you perhaps hear later on that he had worked as a police inspector in Vukovar before the war?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-009 [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. But I heard that he was a judge or some kind of judge, whatever it is.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOMAZET
utterances.text: Did you perhaps know that Zigic was the father-in-law of Vujanovic whom you met later on?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-009 [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, sir, I wasn't aware of that, no.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOMAZET
utterances.text: While answering my learned friend's questions you used that photograph to show us a couple of things. You marked the spot where the military trucks got their fuel within the Velepromet compound. You must know, because you told us about this, that the JNA barracks was near the Velepromet compound. My question: Do you perhaps know if JNA vehicles also -- whether JNA vehicles got their fuel in their own barracks, which wasn't far from Velepromet?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-009 [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's possible, sir, but where I was over there, at that point of time, I have seen trucks coming in and getting some of them refueled or getting some supplies from that warehouse. But were they using barracks for that kind of stuff, I was a prisoner at that point, so I have no idea, and I couldn't see it, if they did or not.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOMAZET
utterances.text: Bearing this in mind, would you allow for the possibility, based on what you could see, that Territorial Defence lorries were getting their supplies from the Velepromet compound, and that this term that you used, "military vehicles," could also be applied to the vehicles used by Vukovar's TO?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-009 [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's -- that's correct. That could be possibility, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOMAZET
utterances.text: You spoke about the guards at the Velepromet entrance. You said those were military policemen, and you could tell them because they -- they all had white belts. My question: I think you spoke about their uniforms. These were olive-drab JNA uniforms with white belts and this indicated to you that these persons were military policemen. Am I right?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-009 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yeah, you could be right. That's right, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOMAZET
utterances.text: Can you remember if those military policemen that you saw at the entrance to Velepromet had white belts -- I mean only white belts, or also those white belts worn over the shoulder, the kind that is usually worn around the waist, but there is the other kind that is usually worn from the shoulder down to the belt. Do you remember these military policemen wearing those belts, too, or just the ones around the waist?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-009 [Resumed]
utterances.text: If I remember correctly, I think they only had belts. I don't remember having that, no.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOMAZET
utterances.text: Thank you. Just another question about this. Do you know, or do you not know, if Vukovar's Territorial Defence had its own police force?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-009 [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, I'm not sure about that. I cannot say that for sure. But I've seen people from a Territorial Defence having belts on them, white belts, but that's a possibility. I'm not sure. I can't answer that with yes, no.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOMAZET
utterances.text: Thank you. You spoke about the time you spent at Petrova Gora. You spoke about that kitchen that you used to go to. You probably know this, so I'm going to ask you this: In addition to catering for the TO people and those who were fighting there, did the kitchen cater also for the population of that area?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-009 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, sir. That was a public kitchen for everybody, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOMAZET
utterances.text: Thank you. You described to us what was going on at the time. I think it was on the 17th of November that person B brought to that house a lady who had previously been in the centre of Vukovar in a cellar and who said that several days before she had obtained some supplies from the Nama department store. She said that it was possible to buy some things there, and you found that exceptionally strange. While testifying in chief, you talked about the heavy shelling on account of which people were -- were not able to move about out in the open. My question is: What you found to be exceptionally strange, were you surprised by the fact that in the centre of town itself there was a shop open that was selling supplies? This probably did not apply to other parts of Vukovar or any of the parts of Vukovar that you had been to at least?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-009 [Resumed]
utterances.text: First of all, it wasn't person B that brought that person in there. That was a different person over there. But, yes, that was very weird that she would say something like that, considering how many shelling and -- how much shelling and how many grenades fell during the day on Vukovar. As she explained in her story, when she went downtown to get some groceries, there were -- it wasn't a store that was working, but there people inside or outside the store probably selling the stuff from the store to people that had money to pay for it. That's the understanding that I got, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOMAZET
utterances.text: Thank you for this clarification. You spoke about your presence when civilians were being separated. You said there was a need to screen them and that the first attempt that was made was to separate Serbs from Croats. The Serbs were told to come forward, and you say that a great deal more people had come forward than had been expected to, and then individual vetting began. Did I understand that answer correctly, sir?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-009 [Resumed]
utterances.text: If you're talking about Velepromet, yes, people were separated as soon as they were taken off the buses or the trucks. One of the questions was that was asked that Serbs step out from the crowd, well, from the line that -- from men -- actually, the question was actually towards the men. And they were asked to step out. A lot of people stood -- stepped out from the line, but at that point you couldn't say who was -- who was who and whatever it is. So I guess they decided, considering all those facts, that everybody's going to go through a questioning anyways.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOMAZET
utterances.text: How did you understand this individual vetting to be conducted? Was your understanding that people would be asked about their involvement in crimes against the population? Was that what the questioning was about?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-009 [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's correct, sir, yes. That's -- that was my understanding.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOMAZET
utterances.text: According to what you saw or heard, was one of the people who were to conduct this questioning the Zigic that we have already mentioned?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-009 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, sir, that's correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOMAZET
utterances.text: Was this one of the reasons that led you to conclude that according to what you thought then Ovcara was another possible collection centre? Is that how I can understand your explanation of yesterday?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-009 [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's correct, sir. That's -- that was my general understanding at that time, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOMAZET
utterances.text: In your testimony, however, you said that there were certain civilians, and I seem to remember you mentioned a woman, I'm referring to the local population, who were very tense and afraid that all the prisoners would be taken to Sremska Mitrovica without being previously checked?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-009 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't remember saying Sremska Mitrovica, but, yes, that's correct, what you said, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOMAZET
utterances.text: When you heard the way those people responded, did you hear that among them there was a conviction that some of these prisoners had actually committed crimes and that they suspected them of doing so, or were even convinced that they had done so?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-009 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, sir. But I -- I didn't -- I didn't -- I didn't see it myself. You know, that there would be stories or rumours that people -- sometimes people would just come up with all kinds of stories. So, yeah, that's a possibility, yes. Because none of those people -- or I -- that's my opinion. None of -- a lot of us didn't -- were not in a town or inside a town where those things were happening, so those were the stories that people heard.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOMAZET
utterances.text: Did this create a tense atmosphere among the people who were there waiting to see the prisoners?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-009 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I believe so, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOMAZET
utterances.text: Thank you. Thank you sir. I have competed my cross-examination.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOMAZET
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Thank you very much, Mr. Domazet. Ms. Tapuskovic.

utterances.speaker: MS. TAPUSKOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: MS. TAPUSKOVIC
utterances.text: Good morning to all. I cannot see the witness from where I am standing, but I hope we shall be able to carry out the cross-examination anyway. No problem. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: I think that's improved the scenery. Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. TAPUSKOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: MS. TAPUSKOVIC
utterances.text: Good morning, sir. My name is Mira Tapuskovic. I am one of the Defence counsel for Miroslav Radic, and I will take only about 15 minutes, I believe, for your cross-examination. I will try to be expeditious to meet everybody's requirements. Yesterday in answer to a question put by my colleague, Mr. Domazet, you described how in 1991 or 1992 you submitted a request to change your last name. Did you do this in Vukovar?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-009 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yeah, that's correct.

utterances.speaker: MS. TAPUSKOVIC
utterances.text: Can you tell us to what body in Vukovar you submitted this request?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-009 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Municipality.

utterances.speaker: MS. TAPUSKOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, can we move into private session for a while?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Private.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: We're back in open session, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: MS. TAPUSKOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you. Could the usher please put on the ELMO Exhibit 277 which we all saw yesterday. 277 in e-court, please.

utterances.speaker: MS. TAPUSKOVIC
utterances.text: And, while we are waiting for the document to show up on the monitors, I'll put my question to you. Yesterday you told us that the wife of person B found your grandmother in Velepromet; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-009 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Just one second. Yes. That's correct.

utterances.speaker: MS. TAPUSKOVIC
utterances.text: You also told us that you spoke to your grandmother in Velepromet, is that correct, when you found her?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-009 [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's right.

utterances.speaker: MS. TAPUSKOVIC
utterances.text: Yes. Do you have Exhibit 277 on the screen now?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-009 [Resumed]
utterances.text: [Previous translation continues] ...

utterances.speaker: MS. TAPUSKOVIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Yesterday you told us, if I remember correctly, that the shape you drew here and marked C represents where the women were standing in front of this building in Velepromet; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-009 [Resumed]
utterances.text: [Previous translation continues] ... described it, it's when people are taken off the bus, that's where women would stand and men were taken away and put in lines. And that's correct, that's what C represents.

utterances.speaker: MS. TAPUSKOVIC
utterances.text: Very well. You told us that your grandmother was in the building that you have marked G; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-009 [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's correct. I'm sorry -- okay, go ahead.

utterances.speaker: MS. TAPUSKOVIC
utterances.text: You also told us here that you spoke to your grandmother outside in front of the hangar?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-009 [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's right.

utterances.speaker: MS. TAPUSKOVIC
utterances.text: As you have described and marked on this photograph, this position of all the persons who were in Velepromet at the time, can you explain to us how it came about that your grandmother was in G and how she was able to come outside to talk to you?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-009 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't understand the question, I'm sorry. What do you mean, how was she over there?

utterances.speaker: MS. TAPUSKOVIC
utterances.text: I'll try to simplify my question. Can you explain how your grandmother was able to come out of the building you have marked G, although it was being guarded, and talked to you outside the building?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-009 [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's more understandable to me. Person B's wife managed to get her out and to talk to me for a couple of minutes, yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. TAPUSKOVIC
utterances.text: Thank you. On the first day of your testimony when asked by my learned friend from the Office of the Prosecutor, you said that your grandparents were taken to Sremska Mitrovica from Velepromet; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-009 [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's correct, yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. TAPUSKOVIC
utterances.text: In your statement to the investigators of the Tribunal in 1998 you said that your mother invested a lot of effort into getting them out of Sremska Mitrovica; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-009 [Resumed]
utterances.text: She went over there to see them. She got my grandmother from there; she was released. My grandfather stayed in the prison and he was released later as a war prisoner, or whatever the exchange was happening later on, yes. That's correct.

utterances.speaker: MS. TAPUSKOVIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Can you then explain the fact that we received from the Tribunal a list compiled by the government of the Republic of Croatia the Commission for Detainees and Missing Persons, and this is a list of all the persons who were in Sremska Mitrovica and who were exchanged or released on any basis, and that this list includes neither the name of your grandmother nor the name of your grandfather. So I will repeat my question. Can you explain this?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-009 [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, I don't. I don't have it.

utterances.speaker: MS. TAPUSKOVIC
utterances.text: Thank you. We'll now move on to the events of the 20th of November. You said that you saw person D at Ovcara and that you knew him from your school days; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-009 [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's correct.

utterances.speaker: MS. TAPUSKOVIC
utterances.text: Could the usher remove this photograph, please? We don't need it anymore. You said that you spoke to person D about some family problems of yours; do you remember that?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-009 [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, I don't remember that. No.

utterances.speaker: MS. TAPUSKOVIC
utterances.text: You don't remember that you mentioned to person D that your grandparents were killed in Pionirska Street?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-009 [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. But that's where they used to live. No.

utterances.speaker: MS. TAPUSKOVIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Could the usher now put on e-court Exhibit 156, please? And while we are waiting for the photograph to come up on the monitors, it's a photograph you saw yesterday, I'll move on and ask you my next question. You told us here that on the 7th of November, 1991 you were approached by Zarko Amidzic; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-009 [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's correct, yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. TAPUSKOVIC
utterances.text: And in your conversation with him he insisted that you join the TO?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-009 [Resumed]
utterances.text: And that's correct, too.

utterances.speaker: MS. TAPUSKOVIC
utterances.text: And person B opposed what Amidzic was insisting on; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-009 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yeah. He didn't want me to join anything, yes Not at that point, no.

utterances.speaker: MS. TAPUSKOVIC
utterances.text: But regardless of the opposition of person B, you gave way to pressure from Zarko Amidzic and you went to another building to formally join the TO; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-009 [Resumed]
utterances.text: That is correct, yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. TAPUSKOVIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Could the usher now assist the witness with a pen. And, sir, if we could zoom in on the map by two positions, if possible. Once more, please. Thank you. Could you indicate the approximate location of the building where it was, where you reported to join the TO. If it's a problem, we can try to zoom in further.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-009 [Resumed]
utterances.text: This is the house where we stayed. This pen is not working. It's not working. The pen is not working, I cannot. No. The pen is not working, I can't.

utterances.speaker: MS. TAPUSKOVIC
utterances.text: We will continue with our questions while this technical problem is being solved. Can you tell me -- we'll move on to save time, and if the smart pen or smart screen can be made to work, then we'll come back to this. Please tell us how far the house where you registered as a member of TO was from the house in which you were living with person B?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-009 [Resumed]
utterances.text: It was about three to five minutes walk, not -- not even that, no.

utterances.speaker: MS. TAPUSKOVIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Tell me, please, do you know the name of the street in which the house inhabited by person B was? And just say yes or no at this point. Don't mention the name of the street.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-009 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yeah, I think I know. I think I know.

utterances.speaker: MS. TAPUSKOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, may we move into private session for a minute?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Private.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: We are in open session, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MS. TAPUSKOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MS. TAPUSKOVIC
utterances.text: I wanted you to mark on the map some other things, but we shall see. Tell me, then, the place where the wife of person B worked, how far away was that from the house in which you were staying? That was the house where person B lived.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-009 [Resumed]
utterances.text: It was about five minutes. It was in the same street, where the house was. Yeah.

utterances.speaker: MS. TAPUSKOVIC
utterances.text: And tell me, the public -- the soup-kitchen where you were eating, how far away was it from the place where you were staying?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-009 [Resumed]
utterances.text: It was the same house where I -- where I was brought first time to get dressed.

utterances.speaker: MS. TAPUSKOVIC
utterances.text: And the house where you registered and took a uniform and where you were given weapons?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-009 [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's correct, yeah.

utterances.speaker: MS. TAPUSKOVIC
utterances.text: Can you tell us as you spent the time period from the 4th -- 4th of November until the fall of Vukovar and a few more days there, can you tell us whether there were any positions of the TO on Petrova Gora and whether the TO had certain weapons there and, if so, what weapons?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-009 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I'm not sure -- I don't think they had any positions over there. As far as keeping the weapons or -- I don't know, or some kind of weaponry, as you're talking about, no, I wasn't aware of that. No.

utterances.speaker: MS. TAPUSKOVIC
utterances.text: Very well. Thank you. Can we proceed? We'll go back now, sir. Please try to mark on this photograph the house where you were staying. That is the house --

utterances.speaker: MS. TAPUSKOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, I think that perhaps we should move into private session.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Private.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: We are in open session, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: MS. TAPUSKOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MS. TAPUSKOVIC
utterances.text: While testifying in chief and while answering questions by my learned friend, Mr. Domazet, you said you did not know who your natural father was; is that right?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-009 [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MS. TAPUSKOVIC
utterances.text: You testified at the Milosevic trial, and you said there that you did not know at all whether your natural father was alive. Do you remember that?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-009 [Resumed]
utterances.text: [Previous translation continues] ...

utterances.speaker: MS. TAPUSKOVIC
utterances.text: Have you learned anything new since?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-009 [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, I don't know where he is. Or is he alive or not.

utterances.speaker: MS. TAPUSKOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, something about the transcript. On page 22, line 12, the answer was not recorded. But a later answer indicates clearly what the answer would have been, and I don't think that really constitutes a problem.

utterances.speaker: MS. TAPUSKOVIC
utterances.text: While testifying in chief, Witness, you said that person B was a close friend of your family before the war, right?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-009 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. He knew my family, yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. TAPUSKOVIC
utterances.text: You testified in chief on page 32, lines 10 through 12, that person B was a very, very good friend of your natural father. Do you remember saying that, sir?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-009 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I do remember that. Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. TAPUSKOVIC
utterances.text: Do you believe that person B knew more about your father than you did, and did person B consider himself to be his good friend?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-009 [Resumed]
utterances.text: He knew my mom and he knew my dad, my physical dad, or biological dad, if you want to call it or whatever you want, when they were young. They grew up together, so -- exactly. And when they -- my parents, I guess, they got married, and I was born. When they separated, I don't know what they did after that, but until that time they knew each other very well, yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. TAPUSKOVIC
utterances.text: Thank you. You said that person B got killed in a car crash. Do you remember when this occurred?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-009 [Resumed]
utterances.text: It was, I think, August or September 1992.

utterances.speaker: MS. TAPUSKOVIC
utterances.text: What about person B's wife? Did she continue to live in Vukovar with her children?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-009 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. TAPUSKOVIC
utterances.text: Thank you. I will now move on to the 20th of November. You said you all got up very early on that particular day. You got up at around 6.00 a.m., didn't you?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-009 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yeah, approximately that time, yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. TAPUSKOVIC
utterances.text: You also suggested that person B had already left and was back at about 9.00 a.m.; is that right?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-009 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yeah, he went out and came back. Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. TAPUSKOVIC
utterances.text: Person B had a private vehicle, didn't he?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-009 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, he did. Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. TAPUSKOVIC
utterances.text: Can you tell us whether that car displayed any damage after three months of fighting in Vukovar?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-009 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I think it was. Yes, I think it was, yeah.

utterances.speaker: MS. TAPUSKOVIC
utterances.text: At any rate, it was still roadworthy, wasn't it?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-009 [Resumed]
utterances.text: [Previous translation continues] ...

utterances.speaker: MS. TAPUSKOVIC
utterances.text: Was this car kept in a garage? Or was it parked outside on the street?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-009 [Resumed]
utterances.text: One car he had, yes, I think it was parked outside; and the other one, the one that he was driving most of the time, he found it on the street. Yeah.

utterances.speaker: MS. TAPUSKOVIC
utterances.text: Thank you. I will now list all the locations that you visited with person B on that day in the order indicated previously by your testimony. After your morning coffee you first went to Velepromet, didn't you?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-009 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Correct.

utterances.speaker: MS. TAPUSKOVIC
utterances.text: After that you went with person B to the barracks, didn't you?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-009 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yeah, we drove by. Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. TAPUSKOVIC
utterances.text: You went back to Petrova Gora, right?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-009 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. TAPUSKOVIC
utterances.text: You now went back to the barracks and you suggest that the situation had changed dramatically in the meantime; is that right?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-009 [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's correct too.

utterances.speaker: MS. TAPUSKOVIC
utterances.text: And now you went back to Velepromet where you spent about 15 minutes, as you said; is that right?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-009 [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's when the convoy left the barracks, and we went after that, yes. That's right. Or together with the convoy, whatever you want to call it. We just briefly stopped at Velepromet.

utterances.speaker: MS. TAPUSKOVIC
utterances.text: You then went to Ovcara, didn't you, for the first time that day?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-009 [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's right. Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. TAPUSKOVIC
utterances.text: You briefly left Ovcara together to Petrova Gora with person B, didn't you?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-009 [Resumed]
utterances.text: [Previous translation continues] ...

utterances.speaker: MS. TAPUSKOVIC
utterances.text: Late the same day you went back to Ovcara for the second time?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-009 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that's correct.

utterances.speaker: MS. TAPUSKOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, there's one thing about the transcript, page 25, line 5 reads, "No audible response." The witness was asked the question about briefly leaving Ovcara and going to Petrova Gora with person B. And the witness answered, "Yes."

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MS. TAPUSKOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MS. TAPUSKOVIC
utterances.text: You said yesterday that the first time you went to Ovcara you thought this was just another collection centre, didn't you?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-009 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yeah, that was the general understanding, yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. TAPUSKOVIC
utterances.text: You also said that there were a lot of people following the convoy in their own private vehicles, didn't you?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-009 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. TAPUSKOVIC
utterances.text: So person B and you drove in person B's car and you followed the convoy too, didn't you?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-009 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that's the -- that's the way I remember, yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. TAPUSKOVIC
utterances.text: On the way to Ovcara did you see any other vehicles headed there?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-009 [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, I can't recall. But I've seen people leaving the barracks with their vehicles in the same direction as the convoy, but I can't say they were there following the convoy or whatever. So I can't say that for sure, no.

utterances.speaker: MS. TAPUSKOVIC
utterances.text: That's fine. You said that when you arrived at Ovcara person B parked his vehicle 20 to 25 metres from the hangar entrance; isn't that correct?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-009 [Resumed]
utterances.text: That would be kind of a guesstimate, yes, I think so. Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. TAPUSKOVIC
utterances.text: I'm just reminding us what you told us yesterday. When you arrived with person B, which side of the road did person B park?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-009 [Resumed]
utterances.text: If I remember correctly, on the right side. I believe on the grass or something, yeah. Just on the main road over there.

utterances.speaker: MS. TAPUSKOVIC
utterances.text: Do you remember if there were any other vehicles parked there?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-009 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I do remember. Yes, there were cars, yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. TAPUSKOVIC
utterances.text: What about in front of the buses? Were there other cars parked there too?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-009 [Resumed]
utterances.text: In front of the bus, like which one or -- what do you mean, in front of the bus?

utterances.speaker: MS. TAPUSKOVIC
utterances.text: Well, I'll move on with my questions and subsequent questions may clarify the situation, or at least I hope so. When you reached Ovcara by car -- or, rather, on the way there did you pass a yellow house?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-009 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, we did.

utterances.speaker: MS. TAPUSKOVIC
utterances.text: And which side of the road was that on?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-009 [Resumed]
utterances.text: [Previous translation continues] ... before you make a turn to the right side towards Ovcara. Actually, towards the hangar, let me be more specific, yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. TAPUSKOVIC
utterances.text: Your Honours, I would like to please ask the witness to tell us again which side of the road he saw the yellow house on their way to Ovcara.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-009 [Resumed]
utterances.text: It was on the left side.

utterances.speaker: MS. TAPUSKOVIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Back in 1998, when you gave a statement you told the OTP investigators that person B parked between the hangar and the yellow house. Do you remember saying that?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-009 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yeah, that main road, yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. TAPUSKOVIC
utterances.text: You said you parked midway between the hangar and the yellow house. Would you agree with me that it was midway between the two, half the distance separating the two?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-009 [Resumed]
utterances.text: The question is kind of unclear. But as I said, it was -- it was a yellow house on the left side between -- before you make a turn to the right side, we parked on that road before the hangar. What was the distance between there, the house and the main road or middle, in the middle, it's just -- it's a technicality. But as far as I can remember, we were pretty close to the hangar when we parked.

utterances.speaker: MS. TAPUSKOVIC
utterances.text: Can I have the usher's assistance, please. Witness, I would like to show you a statement you gave to the investigators. Since you decided to speak in English, I will provide you with an English copy. The relevant portion of the text is highlighted in yellow. I would like to ask you to please read that aloud. Since person B name is included in that portion, could you just substitute the real name of person B for "Person B." Yes, just the highlighted part, please.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-009 [Resumed]
utterances.text: "When we arrived, person B parked the car between the hangar building and the yellow house. He told me to stay by the car and then he went toward the hangar."

utterances.speaker: MS. TAPUSKOVIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Can we now please have Exhibit 256 from the e-court system placed on the monitors? This is a set containing 20-odd photographs. The page that I have in mind is 21; the page is 00531251. Sir, can you see the photograph on the monitor in front of you?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-009 [Resumed]
utterances.text: [Previous translation continues] ...

utterances.speaker: MS. TAPUSKOVIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Do you recognise the scenery?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-009 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I believe that to be Ovcara.

utterances.speaker: MS. TAPUSKOVIC
utterances.text: What can we see in this photograph? Can you please place a cross to mark the yellow house that you mentioned in your statement?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-009 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't think it's visible here. It's right here in this corner.

utterances.speaker: MS. TAPUSKOVIC
utterances.text: Sir, the circle that you drew, does that mark the exact location of the yellow house, or could it be further off, passed this point?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-009 [Resumed]
utterances.text: [Previous translation continues] ...

utterances.speaker: MS. TAPUSKOVIC
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MS. TAPUSKOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, we don't have the witness's answer to my last question. He said the yellow house was not visible. This is page 28, line 13.

utterances.speaker: MS. TAPUSKOVIC
utterances.text: Could you now please use a cross to mark what you believe to be midway between the hangar entrance and the circle that you drew at the far right of the photograph?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-009 [Resumed]
utterances.text: [Marks].

utterances.speaker: MS. TAPUSKOVIC
utterances.text: This should mark the mid-point or the midway distance between the hangar and the yellow house.

utterances.speaker: MS. TAPUSKOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, I seek that this drawing be admitted into evidence. This is where, according to the witness's statement of 1998, person B parked his car.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: I can't agree with that last proposition. But we will receive the exhibit first.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Your Honours, this will be exhibit number 287.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: As his statement was read out in the transcript, there is no reference to "midway." It is merely parking between the yellow house and the hangar. That is a correct reading of the statement. There is no "midway."

utterances.speaker: MS. TAPUSKOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, I accept this. It was an overly liberal interpretation of the witness's account. His actual words have, however --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: [Previous translation continues] ...

utterances.speaker: MS. TAPUSKOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] -- been recorded because he read out the relevant portion of his own statement.

utterances.speaker: MS. TAPUSKOVIC
utterances.text: Sir, it appears that the person B told you to stay in the car while he was off to the hangar, right?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-009 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I stayed by the car.

utterances.speaker: MS. TAPUSKOVIC
utterances.text: Thank you. While you were travelling in person B's private vehicle from Ovcara to Velepromet, how long did the journey take?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-009 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't think it's longer than 15 minutes.

utterances.speaker: MS. TAPUSKOVIC
utterances.text: And it would have taken you as long to drive back to Ovcara, wouldn't it?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-009 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. TAPUSKOVIC
utterances.text: Can you explain why it is that you both went to Petrova Gora afterwards? Why didn't you simply stay at Ovcara?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-009 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I didn't feel comfortable staying there myself.

utterances.speaker: MS. TAPUSKOVIC
utterances.text: I have two or three questions to go. Let us now go back to your second time at Ovcara. You told us about those persons that person B had taken outside the hangar and person D whom you yourself had taken outside the hangar. You found them all in the same spot, 30 minutes later when you came back, right?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-009 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, they were outside. Yes. As far as I could remember, yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. TAPUSKOVIC
utterances.text: Can you tell us what changed over those 30 minutes outside the hangar?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-009 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I -- I don't understand the question. Can you clarify that, please?

utterances.speaker: MS. TAPUSKOVIC
utterances.text: Yes, I can. Was the number of persons and vehicles the same when you returned with person B as before?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-009 [Resumed]
utterances.text: It's a possibility there were more vehicles there, but I -- I can only speculate about it. I'm not sure. I wasn't paying attention to that.

utterances.speaker: MS. TAPUSKOVIC
utterances.text: It was beginning to get dark, right?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-009 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yeah, that would be correct, yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. TAPUSKOVIC
utterances.text: Outside the hangar you saw a tractor with a trailer covered by a tarpaulin, right?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-009 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yeah, that was brought after we arrived.

utterances.speaker: MS. TAPUSKOVIC
utterances.text: Can you tell us who drove that tractor up?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-009 [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. No, and -- no, I don't know. No.

utterances.speaker: MS. TAPUSKOVIC
utterances.text: Can you tell us how far the tractor with the trailer was from the hangar itself?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-009 [Resumed]
utterances.text: The trailer, I think, was facing -- or side of the trailer was facing the main entrance of the other hangar, if I remember correctly.

utterances.speaker: MS. TAPUSKOVIC
utterances.text: My last question: Before you left Ovcara, did you notice that anyone had boarded that trailer?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-009 [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, ma'am. No.

utterances.speaker: MS. TAPUSKOVIC
utterances.text: Thank you very much, sir.

utterances.speaker: MS. TAPUSKOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] This concludes my cross-examination, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Thank you very much. It was a longish quarter of an hour. We will adjourn now and have a 20-minute break and resume at 10 minutes to 11.00.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Mr. Lukic.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Five minutes more, Your Honour. [Interpretation] Good morning, Your Honours. Good morning to all.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Good morning, Witness. I am Novak Lukic, attorney-at-law, and I will put questions to you on behalf of Mr. Sljivancanin as his defence counsel.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Could we move into private session for a while, please.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Private.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: We are back in open session, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: I gained the impression when you were describing Zigic in Velepromet that he was some kind of important person. Did you have this impression that he was not only questioning people, but that he was asked about people's status?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-009 [Resumed]
utterances.text: That was my general understanding, yes, sir.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: You described a conversation between person B and Zigic about your release, and that they had some kind of heated discussion. Did I understand that correctly in your statement on page 27 and yesterday's testimony? Did you hear that conversation or did you only learn about it later on?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-009 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Person B later explained to me that they had really difficult time to take me out of there, yes. He explained to me. I didn't hear the conversation, no.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Just a moment. You said that person B was in the Territorial Defence and that he didn't have any particular position or status in your view. Based on that discussion of theirs, as you also mention in your statement, when you say that Zigic gave way, did person B enjoy some kind of authority and respect in the town?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-009 [Resumed]
utterances.text: He knew a lot of people, yeah, and I believe he had a lot of respect from those people. Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: When you were visiting Velepromet did you see other people arriving and taking away people, either without any problems or after arguments, pleas, discussions?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-009 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I believe so, sir. I believe so. Again, I can't say, because I didn't -- I didn't participate myself in that, so I -- but I -- I believe so, yes. Yeah.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: May I conclude that they always had to ask someone from the local TO, people like Zigic, in order to take someone out?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-009 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yeah, I think that would be correct, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: You said that you were issued with an old olive-drab uniform and a rifle which person B took from you. Do you remember whether you were also issued with a grey coat?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-009 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I can't remember. Could be. Probably, yes. Or I can't remember exactly.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: This is a military coat such as worn by soldiers, an old military coat, a longish one?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-009 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, it was an old --

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-009 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yeah, older ones, yeah. I got the older uniform, yeah.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Have you heard of a man called Ljubinko Stojanovic? Did you know him?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-009 [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, I don't remember. No.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: I understood you to say that you didn't know Miroljub Vujovic and Stanko Vujanovic before the war; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-009 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that's correct, sir. Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Did you know a man called Milan Lancuzanin, nicknamed Kameni, or hear of him?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-009 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I might have, but I can't -- exactly sure, no.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: In relation to the first two, what was your impression about B's relation to them? Did they know each other? Did they respect each other?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-009 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I believe so. Yes, sir. Yeah.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: When you were in that part of Vukovar, we won't mention the neighbourhood, did you see Vojislav Seselj come into Vukovar?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-009 [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, sir. I never seen that person, no.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: But you heard that he visited Vukovar in those days, people talked about it?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-009 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Not that I'm aware of that, no. I'm not sure, no.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: I'll ask you about another person. Does the name Marko Crevar mean anything to you?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-009 [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, no.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Very well. You arrived in Vukovar on the 5th of November. When were you issued -- well, the 4th or the 5th, I can't be precise, but in relation to the day when you were brought to Vukovar, that night, when were you issued with a uniform and rifle?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-009 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I believe that would be -- I think 8.00 -- 8.00 in the morning. I believe so, I...

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: The very next day, after person B took you out of Velepromet; is that right?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-009 [Resumed]
utterances.text: If I can remember correctly, yes. That would be pretty much like that, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: You mentioned the character of B, that he liked to help people, gave away cigarettes. Were you a smoker at the time?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-009 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I did, sir, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: There's a discrepancy between your testimony and your statement, so I will remind you of it. You said that all those days until the 18th, if we take that as the date when the fighting stopped, that you spent all the time at home. But in your statement you also said that you went to Milovo Brdo, where the front lines were. Can you tell us how often you went there, why you went there, and with whom?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-009 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I did go over there once. I can't remember exactly the date or the day. It was daylight. I did stop -- the reason for going over there, because my grandmother, the other grandmother, lives in the same street, down the road. I wanted to visit her on the way to that -- to that point, as you described. And as we did, we stopped over there and then we went to Milovo Brdo. We stayed over there maybe for -- maybe for an hour, I would say, and came back. Yeah, that's correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: But there was still fighting going on on Milovo Brdo; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-009 [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's correct, sir, yes. Yeah.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: You said your other grandmother. Is that your father's mother or not?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-009 [Resumed]
utterances.text: [Previous translation continues] ... it's my other grandmother's sister, yeah.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Can we show the witness Exhibit 277 on the monitor, please? This is the drawing you made yesterday of Velepromet and what you saw on the 18th when you arrived in Velepromet. So I'll put a few questions about that.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-009 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't have anything on my screen.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Wait a little. This is the drawing. And on the 15th, towards the end of the day, you began testifying about what you saw on the 18th in Velepromet, and yesterday you made a sketch for the Prosecutor, and you said that on the 18th of November you saw your grandmother, and you saw military policemen at the gate, that you saw the arrival of buses, that you saw a lot of people, the separation of men from women, the taking away of men for interrogation. You said that whoever was a Serb was supposed to step out of the line. You then described how you recognised person C and managed to get him out. And you made drawings of all this; is that correct? My question is as follows: What I have said just now about your testimony of what you remember of the 18th of November, are you sure that all of this took place on the 18th? Might not some of this have happened on the 19th? I'll just remind you -- well, first please give me your answer. Are you sure that all of that happened on the 18th?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-009 [Resumed]
utterances.text: It's possible, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Yesterday when testifying the difference between the 18th and the 19th, according to you, was that on the 19th anyone could enter Velepromet and that people with weapons also went in and that there was a large crowd milling about, but that was the distinction you drew between the 18th and the 19th?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-009 [Resumed]
utterances.text: [Previous translation continues] ...

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: I'll give you your statement now, because in your statement there's a difference, a discrepancy.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Before you do, Mr. Lukic.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Your question was at line 23 of 40, are you sure all of that happened on the 18th. Earlier in your remarks preceding the question you asked, might not some of this have happened on the 19th. The answer is: "It's possible." It's not clear, I think, whether the witness is saying that it's possible that all of this happened on the 18th, or that it's possible some of it might have happened on the 19th. I think it might be useful for you to get that clear.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, that is just what I want to clarify through the witness's statement, because in his statement the witness mentions some things as happening on the 18th and others on the 19th. So without wishing to introduce confusion, I want to clarify this with the witness.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: I just felt you may have thought you'd got an answer you wanted, and I was wanting you to be aware that this answer is ambiguous.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Would you look at your statement in English, please? When you describe your arrival in Velepromet on the 18th, that's page 5, the last two paragraphs, you don't have to read it out loud. It's not necessary. And then look -- look at page 7, paragraph 2, the first and second paragraphs. I'll put a very simple question to you. When you were making this statement in 1998 the scenes of the arrival of the buses, the separation of people lining up, the men on one side and the women on the other, the separating off of Serbs and their questioning, did you link all that to the date the 19th of November, not the 18th? And on the 18th, you only saw your grandmother and person C. Is that what it says in your statement made in 1998?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-009 [Resumed]
utterances.text: If I -- if I can recall the time, then those two days, it was pretty much the same scene on both days. In a -- in the context of all that, these things happened as well, so I did see my grandmother, and I've seen this person over there.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Yes. But in this statement you don't mention the separating of men and women on the 18th, you don't mention buses on the 18th, you don't mention calling out who is a Serb and who is not on the 18th, but only on the 19th. If necessary, we can read out the paragraphs.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-009 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know, what would you like me to answer to that? I don't understand.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: I'm asking you quite simply on the 18th, the day you arrived in Velepromet and found your grandmother, was there any separation of Serbs from Croats or men from women on that first day.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-009 [Resumed]
utterances.text: As far as I can remember, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: My second question: You did not say that to the Prosecutor in February 1998; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-009 [Resumed]
utterances.text: As far as the statement goes, I didn't -- no, I didn't mention that, no.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Thank you. I'll move on. There is no doubt on the 19th it was quite easy to enter Velepromet and you were able to enter with a weapon; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-009 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that's correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Keep the statement; we may come back to it. We'll now move on to the 19th. That's the day when, together with your acquaintance, person B, you went to the hospital; is that correct? First I'm reading from your statement, it wasn't that precise, but I assume you woke up early that day. You say you got up at 6.00, is that correct, most days?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-009 [Resumed]
utterances.text: That would be approximately the time, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: You went on foot, first to Olajnica, and then to the hospital; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-009 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that's correct, sir.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: First you toured the yards of the houses where the corpses were; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-009 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, we did.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Can we see Exhibit 278 for a while on the monitor? This is your drawing yesterday of the area in front of the hospital. Can you remember how many corpses there were and were they lined up neatly? What did this look like?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-009 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Okay. That's not visible from the picture here. But yes, I can remember how they looked like. Because we -- we put -- took the sheet off each one of them. And yes, they were all lined up against a wall. As far as that first house that we went into -- no, well, actually that yard. And they were all covered with white sheets. Approximately about -- I would say -- again, approximately, about 20 -- 20 to 30 people, probably. Yes. And as far as I noticed, as I can remember exactly, they would be mostly men over there. Not -- not Muslims, I don't know who translated that.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Do you remember if they had any numbers or marks near the bodies?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-009 [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, I don't remember that, but I know they were all naked underneath, yes. Underneath the -- the sheets they were all naked.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: What about the other courtyard? Were those dressed, did they have any clothes on?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-009 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, they had -- most of them were dressed, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Why did you walk to the hospital? Was there a special reason for it? I realise that the next day for the most part you drove, even when distances were shorter. Why did you decide to walk, and how long did it take for you to get there?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-009 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't think the roads were clear going -- going all the way down -- well, we don't know that, so we went -- went walking over there. But it takes about -- it's a very small town, so it takes about maybe half an hour to walk.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: What you said about not knowing whether the roads were clear, were there perhaps stories circulating that roads around Vukovar were booby-trapped?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-009 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Again, yes, I probably -- I heard that kind of stuff, but the way we walked and the streets that we walked on, we didn't see any.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: When you were near those dead bodies, that's what I read in your statement, you gave a brief statement to a Serbian TV crew. That wasn't in front of the hospital. That was in the courtyard where the bodies were, right?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-009 [Resumed]
utterances.text: There is a correction to that. It was -- there is a police station just before you arrive to the hospital, so close -- close to that point. And it wasn't a TV, it was a radio station. As far as I can remember, yeah.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Let me just clarify this: In this photograph we can't actually see the courtyards where the dead bodies were, can we?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-009 [Resumed]
utterances.text: [Previous translation continues] ... sir, no.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: We no longer require this photograph. Thank you. Sir, can you please go back to the statement, your statement to the OTP? I will ask you to please read aloud -- just a minute, please. This is the English copy, page 6, paragraph 4, the third sentence. "[In English]: When I first saw Mr. Sljivancanin." [Interpretation] Have you spotted that, sir? Please read it out slowly for the sake of the interpretation, all the way until the very end of the paragraph.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-009 [Resumed]
utterances.text: You want me to read the whole thing? Okay. "It was at this time I first saw Mr. Sljivancanin who was standing in the yard of the hospital. I only learned this name later, but at that point everybody around already pointed at him out as one in command of the JNA in Vukovar." You want me to continue reading?

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [In English] Yes, please. Yes, please.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-009 [Resumed]
utterances.text: "I also observed some type of a white vehicle believed to be from the International Red Cross. This was sometimes in the later morning or perhaps in the afternoon on the 19th of November."

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Is this true, what you've just read out? Is this consistent with your testimony?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-009 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't understand the question. What do you mean?

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Do you believe that these allegations are true? Do you stand by these allegations that you just read out?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-009 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I made a correction to that.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Can you tell us what the substance is of these amendments in relation to what you stated originally back in 1998? You amended certain details in relation to Ovcara, not the hospital, did you? Can you please read that out?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-009 [Resumed]
utterances.text: You're right, I didn't make any -- any corrections to this one. But what is the question that you are trying to ask me?

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Possible, really. You testified about these same events to the OTP. What I want to know is what you stated to the OTP back in 1998, do you still stand by that? Or do you find any of the allegations contained there to be untrue?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-009 [Resumed]
utterances.text: [Previous translation continues] ... that I can see here that would say that people pointed at him as one in command of JNA in Vukovar. That's the only difference that I would say as a correction.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: We both have to slow down, please. So this sentence where you say that the people around the hospital were pointing their finger at him as someone who was in command, that's not true after all? It's what you said yesterday, that he gave the impression of being a proper JNA officer. Was that what led you to believe that he was in charge?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-009 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Okay. If you let me to clarify this. When I gave the statement, I didn't write these letters. There was a person that was present in the room when I gave the statement, and I believe, and I pointed out that to the Prosecution, that some words that are mentioned in my statement are not the way I put them. The general understanding is there, but not the way I worded. So if you're trying to go with word by word that's written here, some words that are over there are not the ones that I used. That's all I can say now.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Just let me make one small distinction there, and we can go back to that subject. Do you remember when this interview was conducted in February 1998, was a video recording or a tape recording made of that interview? Do you remember that?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-009 [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, I don't remember. No. I think it was -- everything was written on a piece of paper, I think. I believe so.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: But based on what I can tell from your statement, there was no interpreter involved, you -- you were using English in your interview with the OTP, weren't you?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-009 [Resumed]
utterances.text: [Previous translation continues] ...

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Your last answer was not recorded, sir. The interview was conducted in English, right?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-009 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, sir, that's correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Yesterday, or rather day before yesterday on page 11, I'm talking about your testimony here, not about the statement, if need be we can go back to that, but you said you were standing outside the hospital for about half an hour. You testified about that, and you saw him in passing briefly, you said that on page 11, didn't you? The day before yesterday.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-009 [Resumed]
utterances.text: [Previous translation continues] ... correct sir, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: You testified in chief about his appearance and you provided a lot of detail. The next day you saw him in the barracks or, rather, at Ovcara, was he dressed the same way as the day you had previously seen him in the hospital courtyard?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-009 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, as far as I can remember. To my knowledge, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: In your statement you said this might have been some time late in the morning or early in the afternoon. You told us how long it took you to get there. Was this sometime between 11.00 a.m. and 1.00 p.m.? It's really important, so if you could please specify, this half hour that you spent in the hospital, when was that?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-009 [Resumed]
utterances.text: [Previous translation continues] ... can't say -- no, I can't say. No. No, I cannot remember exactly. What time was it. No, I don't know.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Let's take this one step at a time, please, and try to get as close as possible to the actual time-line. You walked, you crossed Olajnica and reached that courtyard there, you spent some time there, and then you walked up to the hospital entrance, if we can rewind the film, as it were. When did you first set out? Were you in front of the hospital at around 11.00 a.m. or midday, perhaps?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-009 [Resumed]
utterances.text: [Previous translation continues] ... I don't really know.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: What you stated back in 1998, when your memory was probably a lot fresher, might just comprise this time-frame, right?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-009 [Resumed]
utterances.text: [Previous translation continues] ... I don't remember exactly did I say 11.00 or 12.00 or whatever. I -- no. I've said somewhere in between that time, could be, maybe not. You know, as I said, it's possible. I'm not sure. I am not sure. Time-frames are really hard to say.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Perhaps I'm asking a lot. I won't press you on this, because you have been specific enough, it seems. First you took the bus and then you walked to Velepromet, and there was still natural light outside before you got there, right?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-009 [Resumed]
utterances.text: [Previous translation continues] ... the bus. I don't know how you misunderstood that.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Can you please just hold your breath, sir? The interpreters need to finish up before you start answering the question. My understanding is you left the hospital to go back home in actual fact with B, but then you came across a bus on which you drove part of the way and then from thereon you decided to walk and it was then you made up your mind to go to Velepromet, right?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-009 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yeah, that would be correct, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: My understanding of your testimony, please confirm if I'm right, this time at the hospital was the first time you saw Sljivancanin. You had not previously seen him in Vukovar. From your arrival -- or, rather, you had never seen him in your life, right?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-009 [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's absolutely correct, sir, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: And based on an answer you provided yesterday, you were not able to watch TV in Vukovar. You only identified him at Bijeljina later on. You had never seen him anywhere prior to that encounter at the hospital, had you?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-009 [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's correct, sir, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Can you please help us with this, sir: In addition to B, whom you were standing with outside the hospital, did you see anyone else whom you recognised standing there, somebody who can confirm your story about seeing my client there? Do you remember anybody else?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-009 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I believe it was -- he was -- his son, I believe he was there too.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: One of those two, the younger or the older?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-009 [Resumed]
utterances.text: [Previous translation continues] ...

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: What was your last answer?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I think it was his older son.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: A couple of questions about Velepromet in relation to the 19th. You walked up to Velepromet. Let us drop the bus episode for the time being. How long did you stay there at Velepromet on that day, the 19th? I'm talking about the 19th now. You said you stood guard. You even stood guard for about 15 minutes right outside?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-009 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Again, those 15 minutes, that could be -- time-frames, but again, yes, we spent -- we spent some time on Velepromet. That's for sure, yes. Yeah.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: 15 minutes. All right. You spent a short time outside the door of a hangar; would you agree with that?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-009 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that's correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: It was outside Velepromet that B gave you his rifle to keep when he entered Velepromet, didn't he?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-009 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, sometimes he would leave it to me. Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Even if on that day anybody at all was free to enter Velepromet carrying a weapon?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-009 [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's correct. Because I was inside too, with a weapon, so I guess, yes, that's correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Was his older son with you at Velepromet?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-009 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I cannot recall that, no.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Can you remember anybody else who saw you arrive at Velepromet without a rifle and then B giving you a rifle?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-009 [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, I can't recall that, no.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Why did B give you his rifle to keep?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-009 [Resumed]
utterances.text: He just left it with me.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: For a short time you stood outside the entrance of one of the hangars carrying a rifle and a military uniform just because somebody had asked you to, right?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-009 [Resumed]
utterances.text: [Previous translation continues] ... Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: You had never previously met this person who now asked you to stand guard for a while and to hold his weapon. You didn't know who the person was, did you?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-009 [Resumed]
utterances.text: [Previous translation continues] ... Yeah.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Can you please repeat that, sir?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-009 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I believe that somebody from Territorial Defence, yeah.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Fine. I'll ask you some questions about the 20th of November now, about the barracks. My learned friend, Ms. Tapuskovic, has asked you a number of questions, you have explained about certain places. Based on what you drew, I got an idea of the general layout, but --

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I believe this would require us to go into private session, briefly, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Private.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Do you remember the reason that you decided to drive over to that man's house just in order to have coffee?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-009 [Resumed]
utterances.text: The reason we used the car at that part, because it was clean, there was nothing -- there was no obstructions on the road or anything, so you could use car if you wanted to go anywhere. Yeah. You didn't have to walk.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Unlike the area around the hospital, which was why you had decided to walk, thinking that there might be obstacles along the way, right?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-009 [Resumed]
utterances.text: [Previous translation continues] ...

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Repeat the answer, please?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-009 [Resumed]
utterances.text: That is correct, sir.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: You first reached Velepromet, you didn't go in. You testified in chief that there were people inside but no buses, and it wasn't as crowded as on the previous day, right?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-009 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yeah, that would be to my knowledge, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Inside Velepromet you saw some TO men, right?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-009 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yeah, you can see -- yeah, soldiers, yeah.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Can you remember who told you that somebody might be arriving at the barracks? What caused you to go from there to the barracks?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-009 [Resumed]
utterances.text: [Previous translation continues] ... on the list. He went inside and he got that information. I'm not sure, does it say B? I'm not sure.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
