utterances.text: We've got it now. At this point in time, did you not find it strange that some of the buses would go to the barracks in view of what had been going on over the previous days and where civilians had been expected?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-009 [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's correct, yeah. That was kind of unusual, yes. I mean, considering that everybody, whoever was evacuated, on to -- until that point, were brought to Velepromet, yes, that was kind of unusual. Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Ms. Tapuskovic showed you something and you agreed, that was based on your statement, I do realise that. But your first arrival in the barracks, in your statement you specify that this was sometime between 11.30 and 1200 hours on that day. Is that possible?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-009 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yeah, the time-frame, I can't exactly point -- pin-point what the time-frame was.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: There is no doubt that this is what you stated back in 1998, that's what your statement says?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-009 [Resumed]
utterances.text: [Previous translation continues] ... I didn't know exactly the time-frame. You know, it's hard to say what time-frame was it.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: The first time you went to the barracks, or rather past the barracks, because my understanding is you didn't actually go in this time around. You were driving. Was there any need for you to enter the barracks or were you actually able to see from outside the barracks that there was nothing going on inside, no buses?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-009 [Resumed]
utterances.text: We didn't see any people anywhere, so we didn't stop. We just glanced from that main road, there was nobody there, so we just left.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: The two of you were on your own, right?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-009 [Resumed]
utterances.text: It could have been somebody else with us in the car. I can't remember.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: You now go back to the barracks -- or, rather, you go back to his house, I'm not saying where it is, and about half an hour you're back, right?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-009 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I can only speculate about the time-frame. But, yeah, it was pretty much shortly after, yes. It could be possible, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: I'm just telling you what you appear to have stated back in 1998. It's up to the Court to decide what your intention may have been. On the 20th were you wearing the same sort of JNA uniform that you had been wearing the previous days?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-009 [Resumed]
utterances.text: If I recall correctly, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: This other time you were not able to drive straight into the barracks. You left the car parked outside somewhere, and you continued on foot and eventually entered the barracks, right?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-009 [Resumed]
utterances.text: [Previous translation continues] ...

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Do you remember what you parked the car with?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-009 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yeah, I think we pretty much walked right away.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Your answer on page 55, line 12 was not recorded. And the answer was "Yes"?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-009 [Resumed]
utterances.text: [Previous translation continues] ... repeat that, yes, we started walking. I'm sorry.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: As soon as you entered the barracks you went straight to this place where you saw the buses, the buses you drew on that sketch. You described that they were parked in a semicircle. At a distance of perhaps about 15 metres from there you saw a group of officers. Among them was my client. And this was outside the circle, right?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-009 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Again, this 15 metres, I -- you know, I didn't have a metre with me, so I couldn't really measure was it 15 metres, or was it 12 and a half. But, yes, the picture is correct. Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Don't be afraid to be specific about distances. You did provide a number of distances to the OTP. You told the OTP about the distances in the case where you saw my client at the hospital and later on -- there is no reason for you to hesitate. Try to be as specific as you can, but my expectations are realistic.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-009 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Okay. If it's 15 metres, then it's 15 metres, yes. Yeah.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Very well. Now we'll take part of your statement again, the one you made to the OTP. The page I'm interested in is page 8 in English, the second paragraph where you describe this. Please read it slowly.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-009 [Resumed]
utterances.text: The second buses.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: "[In English] As we approached."

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-009 [Resumed]
utterances.text: "As we approached the buses, I saw four high-ranking JNA officers standing in the middle of the circle formed by the driveway, not far from where the buses were parked. The only one of these officers I recognised was a Major Sljivancanin. There was another officer who appeared to even be a higher rank than Sljivancanin, based on the insignia on his epaulets. He had dark hair that was greying, and he was shorter and heavier than Sljivancanin. These officers were talking among themselves. At this point in time, the only soldiers I saw in the barracks were JNA, and most of them were military police."

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you. In relation to your testimony here two days ago, there are some small discrepancies here. Now that you've read this statement, does it jog your memory with respect to two matters: As you described in detail, there was a shorter officer with a higher rank than Sljivancanin, and as you approached quite close, could you tell me what the rank was? Describe this in detail.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-009 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Not that I can recall anymore. But I've seen -- I've seen more than one, definitely, of officers over there. Why does it say four over there, I don't know, but what I am saying is just -- there were more than one definitely at that point, and I do not recall the rank. I do not recall the rank, no.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Now that you've read the statement it says he was of shorter stature, or stouter and with a higher rank. Does this jog your memory at all?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-009 [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, it doesn't -- I don't remember the rank, but I do remember seeing other officers over there. I -- no, I just can't -- I can't say that for sure, no.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: You made the statement to the OTP in English; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-009 [Resumed]
utterances.text: [Previous translation continues] ...

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: There was no misunderstanding about interpretation?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-009 [Resumed]
utterances.text: [Previous translation continues] ... as I said, I wasn't taking notes at that time.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Did you read the statement before signing it?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-009 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I -- I think I did, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: And you had no objections, except for the statement you made before your testimony in Milosevic when you reread it?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-009 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I believe so, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: The statement was probably shown to you on your arrival in The Hague a few days ago; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-009 [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's correct, sir. And I pointed out, again, that some wording over there, it's not words that I used, or I can't recall the words that I used for that.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: During your proofing session with Mr. Smith, you didn't tell him that these words from your statement were not correct, the ones about a stout officer with a higher rank that's not in your statement?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-009 [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, I said -- I said that there are some corrections that -- there are some things that I can't remember exactly from there. That I ...

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: But you didn't answer my question. With respect to this sentence, you didn't tell the Prosecutor that this sentence was not correctly taken down in 1998, yes or no?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-009 [Resumed]
utterances.text: For which sentence you want?

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [In English] I will read it in English. "There was another officer who appeared to be even a higher rank than Sljivancanin based on insignia on his epaulets. He had dark hair that was greying and he was shorter and heavier than Sljivancanin."

utterances.speaker: MR. SMITH
utterances.text: Your Honour, I just have a brief objection to the previous question. My learned friend said that you didn't tell the Prosecutor this was not correctly taken down in 1998. I think the witness's evidence today has been that he can't -- he can't remember that, not that it wasn't correctly taken down. It's just a little bit misleading for the witness.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: That was the impression I had of the evidence, and the impression I have of the present point is that he did say to you in proofing that he couldn't remember all of the things that -- today, all of the things that are in the statement.

utterances.speaker: MR. SMITH
utterances.text: That's correct, in relation to some of the wording that was used.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: I think, you, Mr. Lukic and I, all have the one understanding.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Sir, in 1998 your memory was certainly fresher in relation to the events of 1991; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-009 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I would -- I would say so. Probably. You know what, I've been through a lot of hard time, and I try to forget as much as I could. That's all I can tell you. I have been through a lot of trauma. I don't know if you're going to understand that or not, but it's not your point, but yes. I tried to forget as much as I could.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: I understand completely. Do you remember, because you served in the JNA, what a lieutenant-colonel's insignia looked like or colonel's insignia? Do you know whether a lieutenant-colonel has two stars with two frames; and that of a colonel, three stars with two frames; and the major, one star?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-009 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I think I recall that, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: On that day in the barracks you recognised my client on the basis of the impression you had gained the previous day in the hospital courtyard; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-009 [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's correct, sir. Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: There is another discrepancy here in relation to your testimony of two days ago. It's the last sentence in this paragraph. At the moment when you arrived near the bus, there were only soldiers there, the officers and the members of the military police, as you said. Does this jog your memory that the members of the TO and others began to arrive after your arrival, after the first impression you gained when you saw the buses?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-009 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, if I can remember correctly, there were some people as well over there, yes. There was some TO soldiers over there already.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: How many, approximately, people were there in front of the bus at the time when you arrived?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-009 [Resumed]
utterances.text: The numbers, I can't remember, but people were walking around the buses. I -- I can only speculate on how many -- the numbers of people.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: 10, 15, 50? Can you say approximately?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-009 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Let's say 15, 20, I would say.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: That creates an impression, yeah. But in your statement of 1998 you say that when you reached the buses there were only JNA soldiers and most of them were military police; that's what it says in your statement. Do you agree that it was only then that the territorials began to arrive as did other people who were not there when you arrived?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-009 [Resumed]
utterances.text: [Previous translation continues] ... that I've seen military police inside, but I believe there were other people as well over there. Maybe it wasn't -- it wasn't taken at that time, or -- or I -- I forgot to say, I mean, it was a -- two days of giving a statement. It was very tiring for me, so maybe I left out that detail or whatever it is. Or ...

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Now that we are talking about your statement, it says that you gave the statement on the 18th and I think 20th of February, 1998. Those two dates are certainly mentioned, but we never see the date of your signature. Did you sign the statement on that second day, or only later. Do you remember that?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-009 [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, I don't remember exactly. I was shown the tapes, and I was giving a statement. No, I don't -- I don't remember exactly, no.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: When you arrived, at that very moment there was a group of officers near the buses, and among them my client. That's indisputable; is that right?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-009 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I did see the gentleman, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: To clarify: It's not indisputable in my view, only in the view of this witness. And that's regardless of what time it was, but it was about half an hour after your first arrival in the barracks when there was nothing there. Is that right?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-009 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Would you mind clarifying the question? Within half an hour? I didn't understand.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: When you first arrived in the barracks on that day, in your statement you say it might have been 10.30 or 12.00 noon, and half an hour later when you came to the barracks, you saw the officers there and my client among them?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-009 [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's the general picture I've seen over there, yes. As far as I can recall.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Under oath here, and in other cases, you say that when you arrived in the barracks compound you saw my client; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-009 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, sir, I did.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Among these -- or, rather, you approached those officers twice, came really close to them when you were asking to be able to see your acquaintance, whom you recognised in one of the buses. And then when you approached the officers again you wanted to see whether something could be done to have him released. You testified that in the meantime Miroljub and Stanko Vujanovic arrived and that they had a discussion, as you said, with those officers. In answer to a question put by the Prosecutor, you could not remember, or you said you could not hear what they were saying. What I'm asking you is: As you were approaching, I assume you did not interrupt their conversation, because these were figures of rank. What did you hear when you approached them twice?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-009 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't recall. I don't -- I don't know. They were not fighting or arguing all the time. It wasn't like, you know, I tell you something, you tell me something, I tell you, it was going on like for -- right away, right away, you know. It's just -- not when I -- if I recall correctly, when I approached them, I didn't hear any conversation or what was the argument all about.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: In the next passage in your statement you say, and you said the same to the Prosecutor two days ago, that you didn't hear what they were discussing, but that it looked like a vehement discussion between the JNA officers, including Mr. Sljivancanin. If you didn't hear what they were saying, did you see gestures? What is the basis for your conclusion, for what you said?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-009 [Resumed]
utterances.text: [Previous translation continues] ... it was that people were very upset. I probably -- gestures, I can't remember exactly what they did, but I know some of them had guns with them. But you know, I -- it was just -- that was my impression, there was some kind of argument going on. What was it all about, you know, nobody hit and shouted or anything, but, you know what, I don't know. I can't -- I can't recall that. No. But to me, it seemed that it was kind of, I don't know, pretty serious, because it was kind of yelling and stuff, so -- I'm not sure.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: And who had rifles in their hands?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-009 [Resumed]
utterances.text: [Previous translation continues] ... Miroljub and Vujanovic -- and Stanko, whatever.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Did it appear to you to be a conversation between a superior and a subordinate in a military context, or did it look like a discussion among people who were having a conflict?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-009 [Resumed]
utterances.text: It seemed like an argument to me. There was no kind of respect towards the officers, I think. That was my impression. It was kind of, you know, as you say, it was kind of talk between kind of equal sides or -- or -- I don't know how to describe that, but there was no kind of relationship, officer/soldier, or whatever it is, yeah. That was my impression.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: That was precisely what I was asking you about. Do you remember whether any of the other territorials, not perhaps Miroljub or Stanko, was pointing a rifle at one of the officers, or maybe Miroljub or Stanko themselves, that they were not just holding a rifle in their hands, but actually doing something with the rifles?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-009 [Resumed]
utterances.text: [Previous translation continues] ... I've seen people walking around the buses and showing off the guns towards the prisoners, but not -- if I can recall properly. No, I don't think I've seen that towards the officers, no. Mind you, on one occasion I got into a bus, and I spoke to that person, so I was -- I don't know what was going on outside.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: You described a situation where two persons, one of whom you recognised as Tadija Dosen, were pulled out of the first bus, as you said, and that the third brother was taken off a truck, which was parked next to the buses. That's what I understood, right?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-009 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Correction to that would be that I did not recognise him, but I knew one of them from before, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: So you only assumed that the third was a Dosen brother, because you didn't know him from before?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-009 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I only knew one by name, because he lived in the proximity where I used to live, but that's -- that's how I know him, or I have seen him before, but that's -- I don't -- I didn't say that I recognise him coming out of the bus, no.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: The two that were taken off the first bus and beaten, as you described, were they wearing bandages or plaster-casts, were there any signs that they had been injured, and were they wearing civilian clothes? Do you remember all that?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-009 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I -- I would not be able to recall that. Maybe they had something on, maybe -- not exactly, I can't remember. I can't say that for sure, no.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: You told the Prosecutor when he asked you about them, you said that you didn't notice anything special, but that you saw that the third person was on a stretcher. That's what you said two days ago?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-009 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Let me clarify that. Yes, the one -- the person that was on the truck, but not those on the bus. I can't recall those on the bus. I'm ...

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: I was only repeating what you said to the Prosecutor. This third person who was on a stretcher, did he have any bandages or plaster-casts on that you remember?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-009 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I believe so, yes. I believe so. He was on a stretcher.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: I'm asking you whether you know for sure, or do you only believe so? Do you remember whether he was put into the van on the stretcher?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-009 [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, he was taken off.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Did he walk up to the van?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-009 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I'm not sure. I can't recall now exactly. No. No, he was taken off the truck, that's all I could see.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Do you remember whether he had a plaster-cast, a bandage, was he wearing civilian clothes, was he wearing pyjamas?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-009 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Again, I say it is a possibility. I can't -- I can't say for sure. I wasn't -- I wasn't in that proximity right there so I can see exactly, yes, okay, he had a pyjamas or -- on the bottom or whatever. I can't say that for sure.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: And he was taken from the place where the truck was parked to the van and he was taken past the buses, and together with the other two he was taken, driven away from the barracks compound; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-009 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I believe so, sir, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Did you hear later on, as you lived there for a while, did you hear stories that in Negoslavci Arkan had killed a certain Dosen? Did you hear those rumours about how the Dosens were killed?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-009 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Sir, I can only speculate on that. There was -- there were tonnes of stories or whatever. But no, I didn't -- I didn't hear about them, no. After that, I'm not -- I can't recall that I -- that I heard about it, no.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: When the buses left the barracks, the truck followed the buses; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-009 [Resumed]
utterances.text: If I can correct -- if I can recall correctly, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: How long did you stay in the barracks after that? Did you go home first and then towards Ovcara, or did you stay around the barracks for a while?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-009 [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, we walked, we walked straight to the car, and then left after them as well.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, it's time for a break, because I'm a little tired.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: We can't have you performing below your peak, Mr. Lukic. We will adjourn now and resume just after a quarter to.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Lukic.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Just a few more brief questions about the barracks. You said that you remembered that a man nicknamed Faca was taken off one of the buses. He was the brother of a man nicknames Ica, does the name Ivica Husnik mean anything to you? Could that be one of the two?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-009 [Resumed]
utterances.text: It's not Ica, it's Iko, yeah. But, no, I don't know his real name. I know his nickname, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Apart from this episode you described with the Dosen brothers and the one about the man called Faca, did you see anybody else taken off the buses while you were in the barracks?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-009 [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, sir. No, if I can remember correctly, no. Or from where I was standing, but no, I don't remember. No.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: I understood you to say that you moved around quite a bit, around that compound, when you moved around the buses and recognised that man?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-009 [Resumed]
utterances.text: [Previous translation continues] ... around the buses, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: We'll now talk about the events at Ovcara, but there's only one sentence I'd like you to read from page 6 of the English version of your statement made in 1998. When I asked you about the interview you gave in the vicinity of those corpses, could you look at the third paragraph, line 8, I think. "[In English] While he was doing that, I was approached by the female journalist and the film crew from Serbian television." [Interpretation] Was this a radio or a television crew?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-009 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I -- I -- I'm not really sure. I believe it was a radio. I can't believe -- I don't know. I can't recall exactly. I know there was an interview, did they have a camera or not, you know, as I said ...

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Let's move on. We'll go back to the events of that day. You left the barracks briefly to go to Velepromet, as I understood you to say, I assume so that B could report to someone, we won't say who. Was it just the two of you going to Ovcara by car?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-009 [Resumed]
utterances.text: At that point I think so, yes. Yeah.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: The only witness who can confirm that you were not at Ovcara right after the buses arrived is a man who has died; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-009 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Can you repeat the question? I don't -- is there --

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Is there any other person who saw you arriving at Ovcara later on and not together with the buses, in a convoy following the buses?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-009 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know, sir. I don't know the answer for that. No.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: All right. When you arrived in Ovcara and were standing beside the vehicle, you were approached by a soldier who asked you to go behind the hangars to stand guard; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-009 [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's what I remember, yes. I -- yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Were you carrying a rifle at Ovcara?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-009 [Resumed]
utterances.text: At that point, no.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: And when did you have a rifle at Ovcara?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-009 [Resumed]
utterances.text: At no point at all. But at that point, at what you are pointing right now, no, I didn't have it, no.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Did you have a rifle when you entered the hangar later on?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-009 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Not that I can recall, no.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Did you have a rifle when you were standing in front of the hangar, when those persons were taken out, before you left Ovcara for the first time?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-009 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I -- I don't know, sir. I can't recall that. No.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Do you know a man called Mirko Ljubisic?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-009 [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, I don't.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Do you know a man called Goran Mugosa, nicknamed Kustro?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-009 [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, sir.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Do you know a man called Goran Ivankovic, nicknamed Dzo?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-009 [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, sir, no, I don't.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: All right. At Ovcara a similar situation recurred, an unknown soldier approached you and asked you to follow him and stand guard, whereas in Velepromet he was probably a territorial, and now you say he was a soldier, or was it a territorial again?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-009 [Resumed]
utterances.text: If I correctly recall, I think he was a military police, at least -- okay, don't get me wrong, at least he had a white belt on.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: At that point were there other people in front of the hangar when you were standing beside your vehicle? I'm referring to soldiers, not people who came out of the buses?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-009 [Resumed]
utterances.text: If I correct -- if I recall correctly, there were some people, even close to the cars, and there were -- there were some people outside the hangar, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: You didn't know this military policeman? He approached you because you were standing by the car, according to the sketch you made. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-009 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, sir, that's correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Did he call anybody else, or did he just approach you?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-009 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know about that. No.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: When you arrived in Ovcara you described a scene where people were still getting off the buses, you explained people being hit. Did you see the truck that had followed the buses when you arrived there?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-009 [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, sir, I did not. No.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: The Prosecutor asked you about the length of time, and I will tell you that you stated that after the hangar -- behind -- you spent about 15 or 20 minutes behind the hangar and that you then went back; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-009 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yeah, that will be correct. If I recall correctly, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: And you remembered quite clearly when the Prosecutor asked you about the time. How long did you stand there, or to be more precise, were you asked to go behind the hangar while they were still going in, or sometime later?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-009 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I can -- I can answer that. Yes, they were still getting into the hangar, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: 15 or 20 minutes later you left to go back. At this point in time you spot my client, but there are no more people entering the hangar?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-009 [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's correct, sir. Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: When you went behind the hangar, or on your way back from there, did you see in the area outside the hangar entrance any other military officer, before you went and after you returned?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-009 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Before going over there I -- I didn't see any officers at all. Coming back, I did see my -- Major Sljivancanin.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Aside from him, did you see any other JNA officer in that area or inside the hangar?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-009 [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, sir, I don't recall seeing any of them.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: When you returned from behind the hangar, or before you went behind the hangar, did you see any people from that group from the bus being separated off and being left outside the hangar? Do you remember a scene like that?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-009 [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, sir, I don't recall that. No.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: You saw my client, as you say, in passing. As you passed him, it was a short glimpse. You say you exchanged greetings. Can I hear that in our language, please? How did you greet this officer?

utterances.speaker: MR. SMITH
utterances.text: Your Honour, I object to the question. This witness's testimony is not that he had a short glimpse of Major Sljivancanin. He didn't use those words at all.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: We do appreciate that, Mr. Smith. Carry on, Mr. Lukic.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] It wasn't my intention to suggest that. We all know what the witness said.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: But can you please use our language to tell me exactly what you said to Mr. Sljivancanin, if you remember?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-009 [Resumed]
utterances.text: If I -- well, if I recall correctly, I think I said, "Hi," or in our language -- I don't know. I don't know exactly words that I used, but I think I said, "Hi." I did greet him in a certain way. I can't remember exactly the words that I used.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: He was a major who impressed you over the first two days by his behaviour as a proper JNA officer. Don't tell me you said, "Hi."

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-009 [Resumed]
utterances.text: [Previous translation continues] ... again I can't say exactly the words that I used, but it would be more in respect towards that person, that's for sure.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: You go from there to the hangar, right?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-009 [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's correct, sir, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: You spent some time inside the hangar; we'll get to that later. On your way out of the hangar, and later on, did you see my client again anywhere? Let's clarify that first, please.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-009 [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, sir. After that, no, I didn't see him at all.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Did you get into the hangar smoothly, or was there someone standing at the door who had to allow you to get in?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-009 [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, sir. There was -- I don't think -- there was nobody at the door. As far as I remember. Maybe from inside, if I can remember, but I'm not sure. But, no, you didn't have to ask anybody to get in. No.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: While testifying in chief you said one of the reasons for you going to Ovcara, among other things, was in order to see what had become of that man you had recognised on the bus. Did you look for this person inside the hangar? Did you learn anything about this person's whereabouts? Did you see that person inside the hangar? What happened with that?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-009 [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, I haven't seen him in hangar. And apparently speaking to him after all the things that happened, he never ended up in -- in that hangar at all.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Did you look for him?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-009 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I did look for him, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Do you remember what the entrance was like, what type of door? Was it a sliding door, or the usual kind, was it a metal door, a wooden door?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-009 [Resumed]
utterances.text: [Previous translation continues] ... metal door.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: How long were you inside the hangar before you took D out? First as far as the hangar door, and then the exit to the entire compound?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-009 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't think that was a very long time that I was inside. I can't -- again, I can't put some time-frame on it, but it wouldn't be a very long time at all. No.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: You were always perfectly willing to provide time-frames when prompted by the OTP, and yet you don't seem as willing to provide any for me. Some of your recollections seem to be remarkably detailed and some just aren't. Can you please give us an approximate idea, a very rough idea of how long you stayed inside the hangar?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-009 [Resumed]
utterances.text: [Previous translation continues] ...

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: How long were you outside the hangar before you left Ovcara the first time around? What do you think?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-009 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know. Half an hour, 45 minutes. I don't know exactly.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Just to make one correction. Your previous answer on page 73, line 6, was not recorded. You said half an hour inside the hangar, roughly speaking; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-009 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Do you remember when you took D out of the hangar, were there people standing outside already who had been taken out by this friend of yours, or anybody else, and how many people? Can you remember anything about that?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-009 [Resumed]
utterances.text: If I would remember correctly, I think it was three of them.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: What about the next period of time while you were standing outside the hangar? Was anybody else taken out throughout that time?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-009 [Resumed]
utterances.text: It is a possibility, but nobody was put to stand over there, as far as I can remember. That's a possibility. I -- I wasn't paying attention what people are doing. Because people are coming in and out. It was just a big chaos, I would say, at that point. A lot of soldiers coming in and coming out. So I -- I -- no, I can't recall. Or I don't know. I can't say. No.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: While you were inside the hangar, did you see anyone beat anyone else?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-009 [Resumed]
utterances.text: While I was inside I did not see anybody being beaten.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Did you hear sounds of beating while you were outside the hangar?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-009 [Resumed]
utterances.text: You mean when I was standing with these people outside? No, sir. No. I could hear threats, people, you know, kind of -- you know, making threats maybe to somebody, but no, I haven't -- I haven't heard anybody screaming or any -- any yelling that somebody was beaten at that point, no.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Did you perhaps hear the sound of a whistle being blown while you were outside the hangar or inside the hangar? The sound of a whistle from inside the hangar, to be more precise.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-009 [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, sir, I don't recall that. No.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: While you were inside the hangar, and once outside the hangar, do you remember a JNA officer arriving, or a group of JNA officers?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-009 [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, sir, I don't recall any JNA officers at that time. Not at all.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: While standing outside the hangar with that group of people, did you see a group comprising about 10 men wearing clubs and helmets go into the hangar?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-009 [Resumed]
utterances.text: [Previous translation continues] ... No.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Can we briefly go into private session, please.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Private.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: We are back in open session, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: You are testifying under oath, sir. You don't have to answer the following question. It will be up to the Chamber to decide whether you have to or not. Did you beat anyone at Ovcara?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-009 [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, sir.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: If I told you that together with Goran Mugosa you beat person D, after which you took him out of the hangar and questioned him about his possible involvement in combat operations. If I told you that this is what he stated before a Tribunal in Zagreb, then my question is as follows: Do you think you would have reason to believe in that case that he had rubbed you up the wrong way or anything like that?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-009 [Resumed]
utterances.text: [Previous translation continues] ...

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: You didn't beat him then?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-009 [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, sir.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: The previous answer, page 77, line 3, you said no, he would have had no reason. Did you ever clash with D after what happened in 1991?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-009 [Resumed]
utterances.text: [Previous translation continues] ... No, I never had any conflicts with him before or after.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Were I to tell you that perhaps you were part of the security detail behind the hangar, but that what is certain is that you were part of the security detail in front of the hangar and that you were letting people in and out, would you say that I'm wrong?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-009 [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's not true.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Were I to tell you that you were insulting people, calling Croats who were standing outside the hangar with D Ustashas, saying you wanted revenge, and specifically that you wanted to kill a man, your uncle who worked with the Autobacka company, would I be wrong about that too?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-009 [Resumed]
utterances.text: First of all, I don't have an uncle in Autobacka; and no, that's not true. I don't know where you get that information.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: The Court knows full well where I get my information. We have heard testimony before this Court about all these facts that I'm now asking you about.

utterances.speaker: MR. SMITH
utterances.text: I object to that, Your Honour. In relation to this witness being involved in any beating of a detainee, I don't believe the Court's heard any evidence about that at all. There was some evidence about the possibility of insults being made, but certainly not a beating.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Mr. Lukic.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you. That's true. My apologies to the OTP.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Be a little more careful, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Sorry, Your Honour. [Interpretation] I confronted the witness with the allegations of one particular person in relation to the beating. That's why I asked him about his relationship with that person.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Your first interview with the OTP -- just a minute, please. With the OTP investigators occurred in your place of residence on the 17th of November, 1997. You talked to Mr. Dzuro Vladimir, who was an investigator. Do you remember that? This was an informal conversation, if you like.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-009 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I believe -- I remember that.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: At the time he told you how he was able to reach you, that a man from the bus had identified you, and then you talked about the barracks, right?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-009 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yeah. He spoke about the person inside the barracks that I recognised, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: You did not sign any statement on that occasion, did you?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-009 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yeah, that's correct, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Do you remember if on that occasion perhaps you stated to the investigator that you had no idea where the buses went to or was this something that wasn't discussed at all, this particular topic?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-009 [Resumed]
utterances.text: [Previous translation continues] ... No.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Years after these events you were still living in Vukovar. You said you -- you were under a lot of pressure, and you said that you were particularly afraid of people who believed you to be in possession of a certain type of information, right?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-009 [Resumed]
utterances.text: [Previous translation continues] ...

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: You will agree with me that in January 1998 Croatia, Eastern Slavonia and Vukovar were integrated into the Croatian state, right?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-009 [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's correct, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: In January 1998 you could no longer cope with it. You decide to leave town, exactly at this point in time, when Croats were about to start returning, right?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-009 [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, I decided on time, but I still had a job at that time, and I was working over there.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: But this was only a month or so after the investigator had tracked you down, right?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-009 [Resumed]
utterances.text: [Previous translation continues] ...

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: The answer is, "That's correct, yes." Page 79, line 18. Based on your 1998 statement, February 1998 statement, I assume that as soon as you left for this other country, you called the OTP investigator and this is when the statement was compiled that we went through today, right?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-009 [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's when I spoke to them. At that time, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Were you afraid that one of the returning Croats might identify you, those returning to Vukovar, since you had been at Velepromet carrying a rifle, you had been spotted at the barracks at Ovcara wearing a military uniform, and yet all these years, although you were afraid, you kept on living in that same town?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-009 [Resumed]
utterances.text: You can speculate on that as much as you would --

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Would you call my conclusion wrong?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-009 [Resumed]
utterances.text: [Previous translation continues] ... for me, it was -- I wanted to have a better life, for me and my family. That's all I care about, is me and my family.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: That is perfectly understandable, but that's not what your 1998 statement reflects. Let us now go back to your statement, or rather a portion of your statement. Just a moment, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: My question: You leave in 1998. At the time Croats are returning to Vukovar, and Serbs are leaving Vukovar on a massive scale. Wouldn't that seem to be the case?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-009 [Resumed]
utterances.text: [Previous translation continues] ... I haven't seen any exodus of people going out.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Sir, can you just please slow down a little, because of the interpretation? Page 80, line 21, first you said: "You can say that way." Fine. At any rate, the decision to leave Vukovar was formally taken in January 1998. After your first contact with people from the OTP, right?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-009 [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. My initial thinking of leaving that country in total was in 1990, which I was denied, going through Belgrade. And then I always wanted to go somewhere else. And finally I got my chance to do it, after five years applying.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Can we please go into private session?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Private.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: We are back in open session, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I'm about to move on to my final questions.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: You can answer yes or no, please. The OTP investigators informed you that you had been identified by a person at the barracks as someone standing outside a bus, right?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-009 [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's right.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: You were also identified by two victims from Ovcara. They said they had seen you outside the hangar. Did you know about this?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-009 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I know one, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: At one point in time you were standing guard in Velepromet carrying a rifle, weren't you?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-009 [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's correct, sir. Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Late in 1997 and early 1998 the Croats began to return and the Serbs started to leave Vukovar; is that right?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-009 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know, sir. I can only speculate on that. I don't know.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: You had to explain to the OTP, and you did, how you got to be at Velepromet standing guard, how you ended up in the barracks, and how you ended up at Ovcara. You explained that the OTP, and to the Court here, right?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-009 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, sir.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: As for your presence in Velepromet, Ovcara and the barracks, this can only be confirmed by B, who died back in 1993, right?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-009 [Resumed]
utterances.text: [Previous translation continues] ...

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Anyone else to confirm your version of the story?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-009 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I spent most of the time with him. I -- I don't know, sir.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Again, there is an answer missing on page 84, line 8. The witness said: "[In English] Yes, unfortunately so." [Interpretation] That was your answer, right?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-009 [Resumed]
utterances.text: [Previous translation continues] ...

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Sir, I put it to you that you were never mobilised into Vukovar's TO by force. In fact, you volunteered. Am I wrong?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-009 [Resumed]
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, you are.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: And when the OTP talked to you in the presence of those persons - we are in public session, I won't mention those persons - you needed something, you needed to have something to give them, right?

utterances.speaker: MR. SMITH
utterances.text: I object, Your Honour. The question is just a bit unclear.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: I think I got the message. Did you follow that question?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, sir.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I think the OTP got it. I think the OTP understand very well what I'm talking about.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: I am putting it to you, sir, that you needed some information to give the OTP because of problems that you yourself might have encountered and because of the status that you wanted to attain at the time. That was why you gave the story that you did, and this was background against which you placed my client somewhere where he had never been. Is that right?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-009 [Resumed]
utterances.text: [Previous translation continues] ...

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: But the only person who could possibly confirm this is the late B, right?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-009 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I think so, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour, I finish with my examination. Sorry, again. [Interpretation] The answer on page 85, line 9, the witness said: "You are wrong."

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Mr. Lukic, thank you very much. Mr. Smith.

utterances.speaker: MR. SMITH
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour. Just a few questions in re-examination.

utterances.speaker: MR. SMITH
utterances.text: Witness --

utterances.speaker: MR. SMITH
utterances.text: And perhaps we can go to private session for this first series of questions, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Private.

utterances.speaker: MR. SMITH
utterances.text: Witness, you said that --

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: One second, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. SMITH
utterances.text: Sorry.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: We are in open session, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MR. SMITH
utterances.text: And, Witness, it was also put to you that in your prior statement that you believed that there was a white vehicle that you thought may have belonged to the Red Cross, you believed belonged to the Red Cross, at the time that you saw Major Sljivancanin at the Vukovar Hospital?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-009 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. SMITH
utterances.text: Did that --

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-009 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, sir.

utterances.speaker: MR. SMITH
utterances.text: Did that vehicle have any markings on it?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-009 [Resumed]
utterances.text: No -- I can't remember exactly, but it was some kind of white vehicle that would associate -- well, to me that would look like a hospital vehicle. Usually hospital vehicles or medical vehicles are -- were white.

utterances.speaker: MR. SMITH
utterances.text: And that was the basis for you saying that it -- you believed it may have been from the Red Cross; is that right?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-009 [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's what I -- that's what I believed, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. SMITH
utterances.text: And have you got any further information to say that it was from the Red Cross, apart from the fact that it was a white vehicle and you believed it possibly could --

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-009 [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, sir, no.

utterances.speaker: MR. SMITH
utterances.text: And do you remember where that white vehicle was parked?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-009 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I believe inside, inside the compound of the hospital. I believe.

utterances.speaker: MR. SMITH
utterances.text: And if I can just ask you to look at your prior statement, if we can go to page 7. There is perhaps a little confusion, and hopefully it's just not on my part, in relation to when you saw Major Sljivancanin the second time at the JNA barracks. And perhaps to clarify whether or not there is a discrepancy between what you testified to and your prior statement, I think the best way of going it is to read a couple of paragraphs into the record, and I'll ask you whether or not you agree with that statement. If you can go to page 7, and if you can read the last paragraph of page 7.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-009 [Resumed]
utterances.text: "I went with him again, and when we arrived at the barracks it was perhaps about 30 minutes after we had left from Petrova Gora. It was this time the scene changed dramatically. There were now five or six buses parked in a semicircle in the driveway of the barracks. There was a large number of JNA soldiers around. The military police would not allow us to drive up where the buses where stopped, so we parked on the driveway near the entrance of the Vukovar-Negoslavci road. We then walked up to where the buses were located."

utterances.speaker: MR. SMITH
utterances.text: And if you can continue for the first two sentences of the next paragraph, please.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-009 [Resumed]
utterances.text: "As we approached the buses, I saw four ranking JNA officers standing in the middle of the circle formed by the driveway not far from where the buses were parked. The only one of those officers that I recognised was a Major Sljivancanin."

utterances.speaker: MR. SMITH
utterances.text: Is that a correct account of what you -- of what you saw?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-009 [Resumed]
utterances.text: As we walked -- as far as I can remember, yes, we walked inside, the officers were over there already, at that point.

utterances.speaker: MR. SMITH
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. SMITH
utterances.text: And Your Honour, if we can briefly go back into private session.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Private.

utterances.speaker: MR. SMITH
utterances.text: Witness, you testified that --

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: One second, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. SMITH
utterances.text: Sorry.

utterances.speaker: MR. SMITH
utterances.text: If we could place Exhibit 287 on the screen, please. That's the one the witness has marked. That's the Ovcara photo. Perhaps I'll just ask a few other questions while it's being prepared.

utterances.speaker: MR. SMITH
utterances.text: Witness, you testified that Zarko Amidzic asked you to join the Territorial Defence and person B objected to that. And you also testified that subsequent to that objection two soldiers took you to another headquarters of Territorial Defence to get a uniform and a weapon. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-009 [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's correct, sir.

utterances.speaker: MR. SMITH
utterances.text: If those two soldiers hadn't requested you to join the Territorial Defence, would you have done so?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-009 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't think so at that point, no, sir. I don't think so.

utterances.speaker: MR. SMITH
utterances.text: You also testified that there was a few incidents of restaurants being blown up in Vukovar before you left for Belgrade in July 1991; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-009 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, sir. Yes, that's correct. Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. SMITH
utterances.text: And how many incidents do you know of of that occurring?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-009 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I have -- I have heard at least for two, at least.

utterances.speaker: MR. SMITH
utterances.text: And your family was receiving threats because you believed they were because of your ethnicity, Serb ethnicity, and you said threats were received by others. About how many other people do you know had received similar threats to that in which you -- your family received?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-009 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I would not know the number, but I -- again, I heard the rumours, I believe that -- I heard what people -- what people are saying. I don't know is it true or not. But I can only say on my example, because I know what happened to us.

utterances.speaker: MR. SMITH
utterances.text: And you also testified that -- and I believe you were talking about Velepromet, that allegations were being made against Croats or men that were brought to Velepromet off the buses, that they had been involved in war crimes or some sort of crimes against the population. Do you remember saying that?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-009 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, sir. I remember that.

utterances.speaker: MR. SMITH
utterances.text: Who was making those allegations? Can you explain the type of people that were making them?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-009 [Resumed]
utterances.text: It would be mostly Territorial Defence soldiers that were walking around the buses, or -- mostly local people, I would say.

utterances.speaker: MR. SMITH
utterances.text: And you -- once those allegations were made, did you see what happened to any of those people that the allegations were made against?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-009 [Resumed]
utterances.text: They were taken off the buses, and, as I said, most of the people were just separated at -- at that point of time. Women were separated on one side and men separated on the other side. But some people will be smacked or -- as they are exiting bus, but nobody -- nobody hardly hurt at that -- like, as they exited over there.

utterances.speaker: MR. SMITH
utterances.text: Now, if we can look at the photograph on the screen, this is Exhibit 257. On the exhibit you made a marking, which was the one on the left-hand side with a cross. Sorry, it's 287. And you marked that as the mid-point between what you believed to be the yellow house and the hangar. Do you remember making that marking?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-009 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, sir, I do remember.

utterances.speaker: MR. SMITH
utterances.text: And you also stated that you parked closer to the hangar than that midway point. Do you remember stating that?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-009 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, sir.

utterances.speaker: MR. SMITH
utterances.text: And on this -- on this photograph can you mark with a -- say, a figure A, of the place which you can remember that you parked?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-009 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Somewhere over there. It's very small.

utterances.speaker: MR. SMITH
utterances.text: You've placed a rectangle, a blue rectangle?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-009 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. SMITH
utterances.text: I seek to tender that, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: It will be received.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Your Honours, this will be exhibit number 288.

utterances.speaker: MR. SMITH
utterances.text: And, Witness, you were also asked whether or not the four civilian masked men that beat you up in January 1991, whether or not they were prosecuted by the authorities in Vukovar. Do you remember stating that?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-009 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I remember the question, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. SMITH
utterances.text: Could you identify those men, the ones that beat you up?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-009 [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, sir, I'm not able to.

utterances.speaker: MR. SMITH
utterances.text: Did you know whether the authorities ever had the ability to identify them as well?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-009 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Not to my knowledge, no.

utterances.speaker: MR. SMITH
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. SMITH
utterances.text: Your Honour, I have no further questions. There is just one matter that I will speak to my friend Mr. Lukic about in relation to the allegation, but that, perhaps, can be raised on Monday. The witness doesn't need to be there for that -- here for that.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Thank you very much. The Chamber, and I am sure the witness, is grateful to counsel for their efficient handling of the issues. I would thank you, sir, for your attendance, for your assistance in what you have been able to say. And you will be pleased to know that concludes your evidence and you are now free to return to your home.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: We now adjourn until Monday at 2.15.

utterances.speaker: MR. VASIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, my apologies.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Vasic.

utterances.speaker: MR. VASIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] We've overstepped the mark already. Could I just have a minute, please, to briefly deal with something?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: It cannot wait until Monday?

utterances.speaker: MR. VASIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Well, perhaps it could, but I just wanted to set a wrong right, something that Mr. Moore might have done at the expense of my learned friend Mr. Borovic. Thank you very much, Your Honours. I believe that you have received our joint motion on agreed facts. That's the first matter. If you look at that, it is indicated quite clearly that what my learned friend Mr. Moore was talking about -- well, it was not only about Mr. Borovic, it was about a joint position taken by all the Defence teams. This is something we refuse to include, because the point was outside the indictment. This is 5961 on the transcript, lines 21 and -- 20 and 21. Your Honours, I hope and believe that I have been brief enough.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: You've been brief, and we've got the point. Thank you. We adjourn now and resume on Monday at 2.15.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: to be reconvened on Monday, the 20th day of March, 2006, at 2.15 p.m.
